=== DOCS-TRUTH VERIFIED (2026-06-08 via WebFetch trino.io/docs/current/functions/{array,map,json,aggregate,conversion}.html) ===

• contains(array, element) -> boolean — IS the Trino membership idiom; NO array_contains function exists in Trino (Spark/Hive form).
• element_at(array, index) -> E — 1-based for positive index; supports negative indexing (from-end); returns NULL on out-of-range (vs subscript [] which errors).
• element_at(map(K,V), key) -> V — returns NULL when the key is not present in the map (vs subscript [] which errors).
• json_extract_scalar(json, json_path) -> varchar — returns the leaf scalar as VARCHAR (always). Accepts a string containing JSON, so VARCHAR JSON-string columns work directly.
• json_extract(json, json_path) -> json — returns a JSON value (object/array/scalar-as-json); use when you need to chain further extraction or want a nested object/array.
• approx_distinct(x) -> bigint — HyperLogLog-style cardinality estimate, ~2.3% standard error; 2-arg form approx_distinct(x, e) tunes within [0.0040625, 0.26000].
• try_cast(x AS type) — like cast() but returns NULL if the cast fails. cast() raises an error on failure (the safer choice for dirty data is try_cast or the general try() wrapper).
